`cluster/skills/cdk8s_builders/SKILL.md`:
- 'Group variant constructors under one type' now returns the generated struct: no wrapper, no `to_spec`.
- Replace § 'Only when the API is genuinely incremental' with the build-complete rule.
- The 'Construct holding `self._resource`' paragraph becomes: single-object kinds subclass the binding, and multi-object units are composites outside `providers/`.
- Add a section on references, expressing 'declared here vs referenced elsewhere' as producer-declared references.

`cluster/docs/cdk8s.md` § `dependsOn` rationale (lines 102-105): an admission edge needs no comment, because the check computes its reason from the rendered kinds; only an `ORDERING_EXCEPTIONS` entry carries prose, in the table itself.

rejected.alternative: Constructs mixins for pod policy (`construct.with_(Hardened(), Pinned(...))`, proposal A)
rejected.why_rejected: It is the same eager subtree walk as `harden()`, with identical effect when checked. But it adds jsii `IMixin` ceremony (`@jsii.implements` fails on a frozen dataclass), silently skips unsupported constructs where the function raises, and a chart-level call would pin every workload in the chart.

rejected.alternative: A pure `PodPolicy.apply` over `k8s.PodSpec` before construction (proposal B)
rejected.why_rejected: cdk8s-plus always renders a container securityContext, so owning those fields requires converting all 20 fluent workloads to raw, which drops cdk8s-plus defaults and re-selects Deployments that use the default selector. It also needs getattr-based `evolve` over jsii structs (STYLE's dynamic-probing rule) and a `to_json` bridge for CRD pods, and as specified it cannot express Pods that need their ServiceAccount token.

rejected.alternative: Python-side builders that collect values and construct in `build()`
rejected.why_rejected: Works without `Lazy` or patches, but anything added after `build()` is silently lost, and accumulating across charts needs a shared builder object, which is a registry by another name. Passing the whole list to the constructor needs neither.

rejected.alternative: An intermediate model: need records with one renderer each, and an `HttpService` archetype (proposal C)
rejected.why_rejected: It is the parallel deployment specification PLAN.md F forbids, and its own examples already broke the 'facts only' guard (`Database` carried size and storage class). Its per-namespace SeaweedFS Tenant cannot be built where one namespace's buckets belong to several Kustomizations (namespace monitoring holds separate mimir and tempo grants). The archetype silently added default-deny CiliumNetworkPolicies.

`Lazy` raises in typed slots (#8067). A `to_json` override rewrites wire JSON where no reader looks, and resolvers are global. The one recorded use: a JSON patch of a core PodSpec into a CRD slot is filtered by the CRD's generated `toJson`, and a `to_json` override is not, so that route stays available if CRD pods are ever authored in the core dialect.

rejected.alternative: Chart-singleton accumulators and JSON-patch append methods (#8035's `_ClusterGrant` and `Bucket.grant`)
rejected.why_rejected: They are the Python-only emulation of `Lazy` accumulation, with raw dict patch values and a lookup by construct id. Per-bucket grants make them unnecessary: namespace monitoring already has two coexisting grants (mimir and tempo), and loki has its own.

rejected.alternative: Per-pair single-secret stores built from the consumer's chart (`single_secret_store`, proposal A's `SecretCopy`)
rejected.why_rejected: They put source-side RBAC in the consumer's Kustomization and keep a second authorization mechanism beside the roster the owner named as the standard (#7455).
Policy belongs on a function's defaults or in `harden()`. A spread hides which fields are set, the owner has not ratified it, and it cannot reach raw or CRD pod specs.

rejected.alternative: Composite functions returning `None`, with knobs kept for byte-identical output (#8114)
rejected.why_rejected: Callers must re-spell the names the function discarded, contrary to SKILL.md:24. Knobs for one caller are the #7461 thin-wrapper problem in another form.

rejected.alternative: A Flux component or node class that owns its chart and registers its artifact (#7444)
rejected.why_rejected: `cluster/cdk8s/AGENTS.md:98-101` and PLAN.md F forbid it. `RenderedDirectory` delivers the same derivation as a plain value, without a class, registry or callback.

rejected.alternative: Deriving Flux `dependsOn` from what a chart renders
rejected.why_rejected:
The kind-to-provider map already exists (`cluster/validation/crd_layering.py` `OPERATOR_CRDS`), so derivation would be easy, and it is still rejected: choosing predecessors from rendered kinds makes the graph implicit, turns the map into the 'provides' registry the boundaries forbid, and would bury the rare ordering exceptions among derived edges.
The map is sanctioned for checking instead: predecessors stay hand-passed, and a synth-time validation uses it to fail an edge nothing admission-related justifies and a rendered kind that does not reach its provider.

rejected.alternative: A readiness-ordered Flux graph: a unit per concern, an edge for everything a unit needs at runtime, `wait: true` by default
rejected.why_rejected: It is what the graph grew into, and the owner is moving away from it because the tiny units cost reconcile time and I/O (#7094). On devel 1faf6d5f22, 271 of 426 edges wait on runtime state that converges by retry, 101 unsuspended `wait: true` nodes gate nothing admission needs, and one postBuild ConfigMap sits upstream of 118 nodes.

rejected.alternative: A third ordering-exception reason for the edges a Helm chart's custom resources need
rejected.why_rejected: Those edges are admission edges the rendered objects cannot show. Stating the chart's kinds at the writer (`chart_kinds`) lets the check verify them like any other edge, and it keeps `ORDERING_EXCEPTIONS` to #7094 rule 2's two reasons.

rejected.alternative: Kyverno mutation as the source of defaults for generated Pods
rejected.why_rejected: The snapshot and the fleet rules cannot see it, so generated output would misstate what runs. Kyverno stays for Pods the generator does not author.

rejected.alternative: A proactive tier migration, all raw to cdk8s-plus or all cdk8s-plus to raw
rejected.why_rejected: `pod_policy` and the references work on both tiers, so a migration buys churn and selector hazards with nothing gained. Workloads move when they are touched, and new ones follow AGENTS.md's tier-1 preference.

rejected.alternative: Generating `variables.tf` from the pydantic vars model
rejected.why_rejected: It moves ownership of the module interface into the generator, and a relation test between two live artifacts already catches the drift. Listed as decision 14.

method:
The proposal was made in five steps, each by independent agents that could read the repo and run cdk8s in a scratch environment:
- Inventory: ten parallel sweeps covered every shared helper, per-concern wiring, open PRs and your review comments since the cdk8s layer began, planned and foreseeable needs, and what cdk8s and cdk8s-plus actually allow from Python.
- Design: four designers each proposed a complete convention set from a different angle: construct-centric, values-first, an intermediate model, and consolidating what exists.
- Judging: three judges scored every proposal on every need through one lens each: feasibility in Python, fit with your stated preferences, and maintainability and migration cost. A synthesizer started from the best-scoring proposal and grafted in what the judges singled out.
- Verification: one agent per example tried to break it, and a critic checked the whole design against your original request.
- Revision: the Flux graph on `devel` was measured against the admission-only direction (#7094), and the conventions, matrix, decisions, migration and examples were revised to match.
The page is rendered by `cluster/docs/cdk8s_conventions/render.py` from `proposal.json`: `bb run //cluster/docs/cdk8s_conventions:render_bin`.

scorecard.proposal: A. Construct-centric: single-shot kind classes, L3 composites with typed outputs, pod-policy mixins, nodes that read a RenderedDirectory
B. Values forward: declared references, PodPolicy.apply over k8s.PodSpec, single-shot kinds, a to_json bridge in providers
scorecard.summary: The strictest no-mutation model, and it found the key CRD-embedding fact: a JSON patch into a CRD slot is filtered by the CRD whitelist, and a to_json override is not. But it forces the 20 fluent workloads onto raw bindings, its PodPolicy cannot express pods that need a token, evolve relies on getattr, and the lambda assignment fails ruff E731. Taken into the synthesis: (group, kind) stateful keys and named hardening exemptions.

scorecard.proposal: C. Facts model: frozen need records with one renderer each, an HttpService archetype, DirectoryFacts
scorecard.summary: The strongest roster and glue-absorption ideas, plus the real SandboxTemplate embed check. But it is the parallel specification PLAN.md F forbids, its per-namespace Tenant grant cannot be built where a namespace's S3 objects span charts (monitoring), and HttpService silently adds default-deny policies. Taken into the synthesis: the explicit token-mount decision, write_directory absorbing components and configMapGenerator entries, and the synth-time approval check.

scorecard.proposal: D. Consolidate: one existing mechanism per job, harden()/place(), fleet_rules.chart, roster-only secret copying
scorecard.summary: The base of this recommendation. It uses one existing mechanism per job, keeps the AGENTS.md boundaries, gives a disposition for every open PR, adds a pygohcl relation test, and has the lowest migration risk. Its weak spots were cross-module agreement (strings recombined, N15 hand-wired on both sides) and enforcement (fleet_rules.chart can be bypassed). The grafted references and writer-attached rules fix both.
